1. A student strikes a tennis ball that is initially at rest so that it leaves the racquet at a speed of $64\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The ball has a mass of $0.058\ \mathrm{kg}$ and the contact between the ball and the racquet lasts for $25\ \mathrm{ms}$.
(a) Calculate the
(i) average force exerted by the racquet on the ball. [2]
(ii) average power delivered to the ball during the impact. [2]
(b) The student strikes the tennis ball at point P. The tennis ball is initially directed at an angle of $7.00^\circ$ to the horizontal.
[Diagram (not to scale): ball launched from P at height 2.80 m above the ground, at 64 m s^-1 directed 7.00° below the horizontal, towards a net of height 0.910 m at a horizontal distance of 11.9 m]
The following data are available.
Height of P = $2.80\ \mathrm{m}$
Distance of student from net = $11.9\ \mathrm{m}$
Height of net = $0.910\ \mathrm{m}$
Initial speed of tennis ball = $64\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
(i) Calculate the time it takes the tennis ball to reach the net. [2]
(ii) Show that the tennis ball passes over the net. [3]
(iii) Determine the speed of the tennis ball as it strikes the ground. [2]
(c) The student models the bounce of the tennis ball to predict the angle $\theta$ at which the ball leaves a surface of clay and a surface of grass.
[Diagram: ball approaches the surface, slides along it for a distance labelled "sliding", then leaves at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal]
The model assumes
• during contact with the surface the ball slides.
• the sliding time is the same for both surfaces.
• the sliding frictional force is greater for clay than grass.
• the normal reaction force is the same for both surfaces.
Predict for the student's model, without calculation, whether $\theta$ is greater for a clay surface or for a grass surface. [3]

2.text_clean:
2. A container of volume $3.2\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^3}$ is filled with helium gas at a pressure of $5.1\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and temperature $320\ \mathrm{K}$. Assume that this sample of helium gas behaves as an ideal gas.
(a) The mass of a helium atom is $6.6\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$. Estimate the average speed of the helium atoms in the container. [2]
(b) Show that the number of helium atoms in the container is $4\times10^{20}$. [2]
(c) A helium atom has a volume of $4.9\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{m^3}$.
(i) Calculate the ratio $\dfrac{\text{volume of helium atoms}}{\text{volume of helium gas}}$. [1]
(ii) Discuss, by reference to the kinetic model of an ideal gas and the answer to (c)(i), whether the assumption that helium behaves as an ideal gas is justified. [2]

3.text_clean:
3. The diagram shows the direction of a sound wave travelling in a metal sheet.
[Diagram (not to scale): sound wave travelling through a metal sheet towards point Q on the metal–air boundary, passing particle P; wave direction makes 54° with the normal at Q; air below the boundary]
(a) Particle P in the metal sheet performs simple harmonic oscillations. When the displacement of P is $3.2\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ the magnitude of its acceleration is $7.9\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of P when its displacement is $2.3\ \mu\mathrm{m}$. [2]
(b) The wave is incident at point Q on the metal–air boundary. The wave makes an angle of $54^\circ$ with the normal at Q. The speed of sound in the metal is $6010\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the speed of sound in air is $340\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Calculate the angle between the normal at Q and the direction of the wave in air. [2]
(c) The frequency of the sound wave in the metal is $250\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Determine the wavelength of the wave in air. [1]
(d) The sound wave in air in (c) enters a pipe that is open at both ends. The diagram shows the displacement, at a particular time T, of the standing wave that is set up in the pipe.
[Diagram: pipe open at both ends with a displacement curve (displacement to the right upwards, displacement to the left downwards); maximum displacement to the right at both ends and maximum to the left in the middle; point M on the equilibrium line near the right end]
A particular air molecule has its equilibrium position at the point labelled M.
On the diagram, at time T,
(i) draw an arrow to indicate the acceleration of this molecule. [1]
(ii) label with the letter C a point in the pipe that is at the centre of a compression. [1]
(e) Sound of frequency $f = 2500\ \mathrm{Hz}$ is emitted from an aircraft that moves with speed $v = 280\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ away from a stationary observer. The speed of sound in still air is $c = 340\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
[Diagram (not to scale): aircraft climbing away from a stationary observer on the ground]
Calculate the
(i) frequency heard by the observer. [2]
(ii) wavelength measured by the observer. [1]

4.text_clean:
4. Three identical light bulbs, X, Y and Z, each of resistance $4.0\ \Omega$ are connected to a cell of emf $12\ \mathrm{V}$. The cell has negligible internal resistance.
[Circuit diagram: 12 V cell; bulbs Y and Z in series across the cell; bulb X in series with switch S connected in parallel with Y and Z]
(a) The switch S is initially open. Calculate the total power dissipated in the circuit. [2]
(b) The switch is now closed.
(i) State, without calculation, why the current in the cell will increase. [1]
(ii) Deduce the ratio $\dfrac{\text{power dissipated in Y with S open}}{\text{power dissipated in Y with S closed}}$. [2]
(c) The cell is used to charge a parallel-plate capacitor in a vacuum. The fully charged capacitor is then connected to an ideal voltmeter.
[Circuit diagram: capacitor connected across a voltmeter V]
The capacitance of the capacitor is $6.0\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ and the reading of the voltmeter is $12\ \mathrm{V}$.
Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor. [1]
(d) When fully charged the space between the plates of the capacitor is filled with a dielectric with double the permittivity of a vacuum.
(i) Calculate the change in the energy stored in the capacitor. [3]
(ii) Suggest, in terms of conservation of energy, the cause for the above change. [1]

5.text_clean:
5. A proton moves along a circular path in a region of a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic field is directed into the plane of the page.
[Diagram: uniform magnetic field into the page (crosses); dashed circular path with the proton on it at upper right]
(a) Label with arrows on the diagram the
(i) magnetic force F on the proton. [1]
(ii) velocity vector v of the proton. [1]
(b) The speed of the proton is $2.16\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the magnetic field strength is $0.042\ \mathrm{T}$. For this proton,
(i) determine, in m, the radius of the circular path. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures. [3]
(ii) calculate, in s, the time for one full revolution. [2]

6.text_clean:
6. Deuterium, ${}^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H}$, undergoes fusion according to the following reaction.
${}^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H} \rightarrow {}^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H} + \mathrm{X}$
(a) Identify particle X. [1]
(b) The following data are available for binding energies per nucleon.
${}^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H} = 1.12\ \mathrm{MeV}$
${}^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H} = 2.78\ \mathrm{MeV}$
(i) Determine, in MeV, the energy released. [2]
(ii) Suggest why, for the fusion reaction above to take place, the temperature of deuterium must be very high. [2]
(c) Particle Y is produced in the collision of a proton with a $\mathrm{K^-}$ in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{K^-} + \mathrm{p^+} \rightarrow \mathrm{K^0} + \mathrm{K^+} + \mathrm{Y}$
The quark content of some of the particles involved are
$\mathrm{K^-} = \bar{u}s \quad \mathrm{K^0} = d\bar{s}$
Identify, for particle Y, the
(i) charge. [1]
(ii) strangeness. [1]

7.text_clean:
7. The average temperature of ocean surface water is $289\ \mathrm{K}$. Oceans behave as black bodies.
(a) Show that the intensity radiated by the oceans is about $400\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. [1]
(b) Explain why some of this radiation is returned to the oceans from the atmosphere. [3]
(c) The intensity in (b) returned to the oceans is $330\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. The intensity of the solar radiation incident on the oceans is $170\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$.
(i) Calculate the additional intensity that must be lost by the oceans so that the water temperature remains constant. [2]
(ii) Suggest a mechanism by which the additional intensity can be lost. [1]

8.text_clean:
8. Monochromatic coherent light is incident on two parallel slits of negligible width a distance $d$ apart. A screen is placed a distance $D$ from the slits. Point M is directly opposite the midpoint of the slits.
[Diagram (not to scale): monochromatic coherent light incident on two slits separated by d; screen at distance D; point M on the screen opposite the midpoint of the slits, point P just above M]
Initially the lower slit is covered and the intensity of light at M due to the upper slit alone is $22\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. The lower slit is now uncovered.
(a) Deduce, in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, the intensity at M. [3]
(b) P is the first maximum of intensity on one side of M. The following data are available.
$d = 0.12\ \mathrm{mm}$
$D = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$
Distance MP = $7.0\ \mathrm{mm}$
Calculate, in nm, the wavelength $\lambda$ of the light. [2]
(c) The width of each slit is increased to $0.030\ \mathrm{mm}$. $D$, $d$ and $\lambda$ remain the same.
(i) Suggest why, after this change, the intensity at P will be less than that at M. [1]
(ii) Show that, due to single slit diffraction, the intensity at a point on the screen a distance of $28\ \mathrm{mm}$ from M is zero. [2]

9.text_clean:
9. (a) A planet of mass $m$ is in a circular orbit around a star. The gravitational potential due to the star at the position of the planet is $V$.
(i) Show that the total energy of the planet is given by the equation shown. [2]
$E = \frac{1}{2}mV$
(ii) Suppose the star could contract to half its original radius without any loss of mass. Discuss the effect, if any, this has on the total energy of the planet. [2]
(b) The diagram shows some of the electric field lines for two fixed, charged particles X and Y.
[Diagram (not to scale): electric field lines around charges X and Y on a horizontal line; field lines point outward from X, some ending on Y; point P on the line to the right of Y]
The magnitude of the charge on X is $Q$ and that on Y is $q$. The distance between X and Y is $0.600\ \mathrm{m}$. The distance between P and Y is $0.820\ \mathrm{m}$.
At P the electric field is zero. Determine, to one significant figure, the ratio $\dfrac{Q}{q}$. [2]

10.text_clean:
10. A small magnet is dropped from rest above a stationary horizontal conducting ring. The south (S) pole of the magnet is upwards.
[Diagram 1: side view — magnet (S up, N down) falling towards a horizontal ring. Diagram 2: view from above — ring with the magnet's S pole at the centre]
While the magnet is moving towards the ring,
(a) state why the magnetic flux in the ring is increasing. [1]
(b) sketch, using an arrow on Diagram 2, the direction of the induced current in the ring. [1]
(c) deduce the direction of the magnetic force on the magnet. [2]

11.text_clean:
11. (a) Suggest why de Broglie's hypothesis is not consistent with Bohr's conclusion that the electron's orbit in the hydrogen atom has a well defined radius. [2]
(b) In an experiment to determine the radius of a carbon-12 nucleus, a beam of neutrons is scattered by a thin film of carbon-12. The graph shows the variation of intensity of the scattered neutrons with scattering angle. The de Broglie wavelength of the neutrons is $1.6\times10^{-15}\ \mathrm{m}$.
[Graph: intensity against $\theta$ / degrees; intensity decreases to a minimum at $\theta = 17^\circ$ then rises]
(i) Estimate, using the graph, the radius of a carbon-12 nucleus. [2]
(ii) The ratio $\dfrac{\text{volume of a nucleus of mass number } A}{\text{volume of a nucleon}}$ is approximately $A$.
Comment on this observation by reference to the strong nuclear force. [2]
(c) A pure sample of copper-64 has a mass of $28\ \mathrm{mg}$. The decay constant of copper-64 is $5.5\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{hour^{-1}}$.
(i) Estimate, in Bq, the initial activity of the sample. [2]
(ii) Calculate, in hours, the time at which the activity of the sample has decreased to one-third of the initial activity. [2]
